# Exponential cap moments and the boundary of the two-positive variance envelope

This is an ordinary exponential/simplex lemma and an exact boundary proof
for the two-positive section-variance reduction. It is not a proof of
the interior envelope inequality or of OC.

## 1. A product bound for the moments inside an exponential halfspace

Let Y_0,...,Y_m be independent unit-rate exponential variables. Let c_0>0,
let the other c_i be arbitrary real numbers, and put

    V=sum_(i=0)^m c_i Y_i,  P=Pr(V>=0)>0,
    nu_i=E(Y_i | V>=0), i=1,...,m.

Then

    product_(i=1)^m nu_i >= P.                         (1)

There is no restriction on the number of coefficients of either sign.
Zero coefficients cause no exception.

To prove this, integrate out Y_0. For z=(Y_1,...,Y_m) in the nonnegative
orthant the probability that the remaining exponential Y_0 satisfies
the cap condition is

    exp(-max{-sum_(i=1)^m (c_i/c_0)z_i,0}).

Consequently the conditional density of z is

    p(z)=exp(-psi(z))/P,
    psi(z)=sum_i z_i+max{-sum_i(c_i/c_0)z_i,0}.       (2)

The function psi is positive and homogeneous of degree one, with
psi(z)>=sum z_i. It follows by a change of variables that

    integral exp(-s psi(z)) dz=s^(-m) P, s>0.

Differentiating at s=1 gives E_p psi=m. Differentiation is justified by
exponential domination, since psi is bounded above and below by positive
multiples of sum z_i on the orthant. Each nu_i is positive and finite.
Compare p with the product exponential density of means nu_i:

    q(z)=product_i nu_i^(-1) exp(-z_i/nu_i).

Direct integration gives the exact identity

    D_KL(p||q)=log[(product_i nu_i)/P].               (3)

Indeed the two first-moment terms are -E_p psi+m=0. Nonnegativity follows
elementarily from log u<=u-1, applied to u=q/p and integrated against p.
This proves (1).

Equality holds if and only if psi is linear almost everywhere. In the
present setting that happens exactly when the nonzero coefficients among
c_1,...,c_m all have the same sign, or there are none. If they include
both signs, each of the two linear formulas for psi holds on a nonempty
open subset of the orthant and their gradients differ. Then p is not a
product of exponential densities and the relative entropy is strictly
positive. This also verifies the equality claim without a smoothness
assumption on the crease of psi.

### Every omitted coordinate and the full product

There is a useful further extension. For independent exponentials
Y_0,...,Y_m, any homogeneous halfspace event H of positive probability P,
and nu_i=E(Y_i|H), one has

    product_(i=0)^m nu_i >= P,
    product_(i!=j) nu_i >= P for every j.           (3a)

For the first inequality, the conditional joint density is
exp(-sum Y_i)1_H/P on a cone. Its radial scaling gives
E(sum Y_i|H)=m+1. The same relative-entropy computation as above gives
log[(product_i nu_i)/P]>=0. If the omitted coefficient c_j is positive,
the second assertion is exactly (1), with that coordinate relabeled.
If c_j<=0, the conditional probability of H given Y_j=t is a
nonincreasing function g(t). For independent copies T,T' of Y_j,

    2 Cov(T,g(T))=E[(T-T')(g(T)-g(T'))]<=0.

Hence E(Y_j 1_H)<=P and nu_j<=1. Dividing the full product by nu_j then
proves the remaining cases of (3a). These arguments include zero
coefficients and the event of probability one. If H is a proper
halfspace event with both signs, the full-product inequality is strict,
since the product comparison density gives positive mass to the open
part of the orthant outside H.

## 2. The exact two-positive scalar envelope

Take raw section coefficients p>q>0 and -r_j<0, j=1,...,m. Put

    h=1-q/p,  a_j=r_j/(q+r_j),  x_j=h a_j,
    rho=product_j(1-x_j), E=1/rho-1,
    A0=(sum_j x_j)/E,
    L0=(1-A0) product_j(1+x_j/E).

Thus 0<x_j<h<1. If F is the actual cap probability and mu_i is the
conditional mean E(Y_i | sum c_iY_i=0), the exact formulas in
`candidate f942bc6e02fdf1dd`
give

    X=product_j(1-a_j)/rho,
    F=X[1-(1-h)rho]/h,
    product_(i!=p) mu_i=(X/h)L0.

It follows, with no inequality lost, that the omitted-p variance bound
is equivalent to

    L0 >= R(x,h),
    R(x,h)=rho(E+h)
       [1-(E+h) product_j(h-x_j)/h^(m+1)].           (4)

The formulas extend continuously to 0<=x_j<=h as long as some x_j>0;
then rho>0 and E>0. Zero x_j can simply be deleted. The next section
proves (4) on every boundary face where at least one x_j=h. It does not
assert (4) for all interior x.

## 3. A complete boundary-h proof

First suppose exactly one coordinate is on this face, say x_m=h, and
all the others lie in [0,h). Keep p,q and the finite r_1,...,r_(m-1)
fixed, and replace r_m by R tending to infinity. Let

    W=pY_p+qY_q-sum_(j<m) r_jY_j,
    P=Pr(W>0), M=E(W | W>0)>0.

Write F_R and mu_i(R) for the cap probability and conditional section
means for W-RY_m. Conditioning on W gives the exact formulas

    F_R=E[(1-exp(-W/R))1_(W>0)],
    f_(W-RY_m)(0)=R^(-1) E[exp(-W/R)1_(W>0)],
    mu_i(R)=E[Y_i exp(-W/R)1_(W>0)]
              /E[exp(-W/R)1_(W>0)], i!=m,
    mu_m(R)=R^(-1)E[W exp(-W/R)1_(W>0)]
              /E[exp(-W/R)1_(W>0)].                 (5)

All limits below follow by dominated convergence; the variables Y_i
have finite first moments and W_+ is integrable. Therefore

    R F_R -> PM,
    mu_i(R) -> nu_i=E(Y_i|W>0), i!=m,
    R mu_m(R) -> M.

Consequently the actual variance difference has the limit

    R[product_(i!=p) mu_i(R)-F_R(1-F_R)]
       -> M[product_(i!=p,m)nu_i-P] >=0,             (6)

where the last inequality is exactly (1), applied to W with selected
positive coordinate p. No variance inequality for finite R was assumed.

To identify (6) with the scalar boundary, write
X_0=product_(j<m) p/(p+r_j)>0. Then X_R=pX_0/(p+R),
and the exact reduction in Section 2 says that the expression inside
the square brackets in (6) equals

    (X_R/h)[L0(x(R))-R(x(R),h)].

Since R X_R/h -> pX_0/h>0, equation (6) proves (4) at x_m=h. If another
finite r_j is strictly positive, the remaining W has both a positive
coefficient q and a negative coefficient besides the selected p. The
strictness statement in Section 1 then makes (6), and hence the boundary
inequality, strict. If all other x_j are zero, the boundary equality is
allowed and is attained.

Finally, a point with several coordinates equal to h is approached by
points with only one coordinate equal to h and all other coordinates
strictly below h. The scalar expressions in (4) are continuous there,
because h<1 and E>0. Thus the nonstrict boundary conclusion holds at
every such point, without dividing by a vanishing cap probability.

This supplies the entire upper-coordinate boundary of the compact
two-positive scalar problem. Its interior still requires a separate
argument.

The asymptotic argument (5)--(6), with (3a), also proves the nonnegative
leading variance difference for the full product of section means or
for any omitted old coordinate when a negative phase tends to infinity.
This observation is only a boundary statement for those other products;
the scalar envelope (4) specifically concerns omission of p, and no
interior reduction for a different omitted coordinate is asserted here.
